result.scope_note: The claim references a specific standard from June 2022 and makes a universal statement about safe HTTP methods being idempotent. To verify this claim, one would need to examine the June 2022 HTTP standard documentation to determine whether all safe methods defined in that standard are idempotent.

explanation.text: RFC 9110 (June 2022, STD 97) defines safe methods as GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE per Section 9.2.1. These safe methods are explicitly listed as idempotent in Section 9.2.2, which states that PUT, DELETE, and all safe request methods are idempotent. The complete idempotent set is GET, HEAD, OPTIONS

POST and PATCH are not idempotent, and CONNECT is not idempotent, as clearly stated in the RFC classifications. The claim 'every safe HTTP request method is idempotent' is therefore true because all safe methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE) are confirmed idempotent.

The June 2022 standard used worldwide (RFC 9110, STD 97) provides the authoritative classification. Evidence from restguide.info citations with IETF origin confirms the standard's scope and method properties match the claim's timeframe and population requirements.

excerpts.text:
A method is idempotent when the intended effect of two or more identical requests is the same as the effect of one request.

[Section 9.2.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-9.2.2) states that **PUT**, **DELETE**, and the safe request methods are idempotent. The safe methods are GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE.

The complete idempotent set is therefore **GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT, and DELETE**. **POST** and **CONNECT** are not idempotent.
